messages:
Evan: Mercury Health sent their network appendix. POC will hit hosted API but security insists on private connectivity. They asked: PrivateLink vs peering vs Transit GW, exact firewall entries, and whether client source IPs are preserved. Fast answers?
Priya: Short: PrivateLink is quickest for hosted POC (interface endpoint). VPC peering or TGW preserves client source IPs if you need that. PrivateLink terminates at our ENI so backend sees endpoint ENI IPs.
Jules: Add: Transit Gateway can be used if they have multi-account hubs and want to centralize connectivity to us via a partner transit. That adds setup but preserves IPs if traffic is routed into our VPC via peering/egress paths. TGW-only doesn't magically preserve src IP unless the traffic is routed into our VPC in a way that keeps original IPs (peering or direct connect).
Marta: Firewall rules snippet for their netops (minimal):
```
# Allow app subnet -> Redwood PrivateLink (TLS)
Allow: TCP 443 -> privatelink.us-west-2.api.redwood-inference.internal
Allow: ICMP type 3 (PMTU)
# Optional if NTP not managed internally
Allow: UDP 123 -> pool.ntp.org
```
Evan: They said "NO DNS, IP-only". Can PrivateLink meet that?
Priya: Yes: we provision the interface endpoint and return the public EIPs bound to the endpoint ENIs. They can allowlist those. Caveat: AWS may reassign underlying EIPs during maintenance. For strict immutability, peering or a Dedicated/private deployment is recommended. Flag in the questionnaire.
Jules: Also call out SNI: corporate proxies sometimes only allow SNI on specific hostnames. If they use SNI allowlists, give them the TLS SNI host (privatelink.us-west-2.api.redwood-inference.internal). If their proxy drops SNI we need a different plan.
Marta: CMDB-friendly JSON they can paste into a change ticket (replace values after we provision):
```json
{"id":"redwood-privatelink-egress","direction":"egress","proto":"tcp","port":"443","dest":"<PROVIDED_EIP_OR_FQDN>","notes":"POC to Redwood; replace dest with provided EIPs if IP-only policy"}
```
Evan: Pricing blurb for procurement?
Priya: PrivateLink pricing = AWS interface endpoint hourly + AWS data processing per-GB + our connectivity surcharge (small). VPC peering/TGW = no endpoint hourly but potential cross-AZ and inter-region transfer costs and more setup hours. For quick POC PrivateLink typically lower ops time.
Jules: Security Q: "Can you do mTLS?" Answer: mutual TLS is available for Dedicated/private deployments as an enterprise feature. Hosted PrivateLink supports TLS 1.2/1.3; we recommend short-lived API keys for POC and request-level logging.
Marta: Operational gotcha: some customers also require original client IP for application-layer allowlists. If they need that AND only allow IP-based allowlists, that's tricky: PrivateLink + IP allowlist is possible, but src-IP won't be preserved. Peering/Dedicated preserves it. Call that an architecture decision for sales to escalate.
Evan: Action items: (1) Ask Mercury to confirm IP-only vs DNS/SNI ok, (2) ask for expected GB/day, (3) if IP-only ask infra to provision sandbox interface endpoint and we'll share EIPs.
infra-bot: Ticket NET-22011 created to provision sandbox PrivateLink in us-west-2 for Mercury Health POC. Owner: infra-oncall. ETA 48 hours.
Evan: Thanks all thumbsup
